title: Tuned chimes
summary: a chime in tune before you cut it
description: A wind chime of tubes, or a glockenspiel of bars, cut to pitch from the free-free beam formula: pick the scale and the stock you bought, get every length and node hole, a full-size cut-and-drill sheet, and a form that corrects itself from a tuner reading of your own test piece.
process: Tubes or flat bars cut and drilled by hand; oak disc turned or routed; laser or paper template for the cut sheet

difficulty.rationale: Coupled per-note beam physics with a fitted Timoshenko closed form, two instruments, a drive slider, a cut sheet and kernel limits over the range.

standards: Free-free beam first mode: Tom Irvine, Bending Frequencies of Bernoulli-Euler Beams, rev. W (2026), Table 1 and Appendix H (read): beta L = 4.73004, 22.373
Timoshenko correction, closed form fitted to and checked against a shooting-method solver; shear coefficient: Cowper (1966) as tabulated in Wikipedia, Timoshenko-Ehrenfest beam theory (read)

Lee Hite, Tubular Bell Chimes Do-It-Yourself Compendium (2022), read: 22.4 % node (p. 20 and p. 24), cut long and deburr (Step 3, p. 8), alignment and striker (Steps 13 and 17, p. 11), tuning caution (pp. 24 to 25)
EN 1999-1-1 section 3.2.5: aluminium E 70 000, G 27 000 N/mm2, 2 700 kg/m3 (read)
EN 1993-1-1 section 3.2.6 via eurocodeapplied.com: E 210 000 MPa, G 81 000 MPa (read)
Equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz (the tuning reference, my statement)
materials: Aluminium tube (default 25 x 1.5 mm); or mild or stainless steel, brass, copper; or flat bar
Oak top disc and sail, turned walnut striker
Waxed linen cord, brass hanging ring
